scope_review.notes: Scope review: tip of Baron Philosophia theologiae ancillans Exercitatio Prima Art. I-III (necessary being; being by essence; actual/potential/mixed; God as actus purus) from the 1658 Oxford corrected Latin, not the whole work. Era disclosed as early-seventeenth-century Reformed St Andrews/Oxford school Latin, not patristic. No explicit Scripture in this tip locus — scripture check is pass as none omitted/invented. Honest tip-to-FULL expand past Art. I-II.

reviews.notes: Compared Pass B to locked 1658 Latin of Exercitatio Prima Art. I. Necessary vs contingent being; God cannot deprive himself of being; creatures hang on free conserving cause. Pass A != B. No Scripture in locus. Spot-check vs IA PDF leaves ~15-16 / DjVu: negation and agency hold. Exodus padding removed (tip exemption).

Compared Pass B to locked Latin Art. II three foundations. Existence of God of his essence; creature existence contingent/participated; essence as potency vs existence as act. Pass A != B. Spot-check vs IA PDF leaves ~16-18: doctrine and negation hold.

Compared Pass B to locked 1658 Latin Art. III. Third division: mere actual / mere potential / mixed; God as actus purus (simplicity; exclusion of objective, passive, and ad-non-esse potencies; active potency as virtus); finite beings composed of act and potency with three imperfect potencies. Pass A != B. Spot-check vs IA PDF leaves ~19-21 and DjVu ART. III block: rosa in hyeme, three potencies denied of God, finite compositions list, and potency ad non esse hold. No Scripture; no ops-leak TNs.
